statement: Find the maximum value of $3\\sin\\theta+4\\cos\\theta$ for real $\\theta$, and the values of $\\theta$ in $[0,2\\pi)$ at which it is attained.
solution: Write $3\\sin\\theta+4\\cos\\theta=R\\sin(\\theta+\\alpha)$, where $R=\\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}=5$, and $\\cos\\alpha=\\tfrac35$, $\\sin\\alpha=\\tfrac45$, so $\\alpha=\\arctan\\tfrac43$. Thus the expression is $5\\sin(\\theta+\\alpha)$, whose maximum is $5$, attained when $\\sin(\\theta+\\alpha)=1$, i.e. $\\theta+\\alpha=\\tfrac{\\pi}{2}+2k\\pi$, so $\\theta=\\tfrac{\\pi}{2}-\\alpha+2k\\pi$. The unique value in $[0,2\\pi)$ is $\\theta=\\tfrac{\\pi}{2}-\\arctan\\tfrac43$.
hints: Write the expression as R sin(θ+α).
Find R and α from cosα=3/5, sinα=4/5.
The maximum of R sin(...) is R, at sin(...)=1.
